page.layout: One printed page. Running head and page number at the top. One text column, with a woodcut of a soldier set into its left side so the text wraps around it. One marginal note in the right margin, beside "Ad Orientalem". Catchword at the lower right and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: que posse duci. Dixi & gemmis ornari. En Trebellius de Gallieno: Gem-mato balteo est vsus. Tertullianum sic accipe, De habitu virginum: Latent in cingulis smaragdi, & cylindros vaginæ suæ solus gladius sub sinu nouit. Par-thi maximè sic luxuriati. Claudianus, libro 11.de raptu.

p.i: Parthica quæ tantis variantur cingula gemmis, Regales vinctura sinus?

main_text.p: Tertullianus, De cultu fœminarū: Vt ex auribus grana nescio quæ pendèrent, quæ Parthi planè per omnia quaque sua bullarum vice inserunt. Atque tales ornatiores baltei, ornatiorum militum. Ideò in Suidā: Μονόζωνοι, οἱ τίμιοι τῶν στρατιωτῶν, οἱ μὴ τὴν αὐτὴν τῖς[?] ἄλλοις ζωσῆα φορῶντες: Monozoni (singulariter cincti,) digniores militum dicuntur, qui non eundem aliis balteum gestant.

»Ad Orientalem aut Tur-cicam formam.] Conspi-ciûtur ita in columnâ Antonini, atque alibi, sed om-nino ratius. Vide mili-tem, qui indidem effictus. An non Græci hoc genus Copidas vocarûnt? Dubius sum, & hæreo an non po-tiùs alio & inuerso fuerint flexu. Ita enim Curtius de-scribere videtur, & cum falcibus componit, libro viii. Copidas vocabant gladios leuiter curuatos, falcibus similes, quis appetebant belluarum manus. Claudia-nus eos intellexit, de lau-dibus Stiliconis libro i.Pag. 179. linea 13.

p.i: —— non falce Gelonus, Non arcu pepulère Getæ.

main_text.p: Ij enim populi, & finitimi, talibus de more vsi. Statius poëta 11. Achilleidos:

p.i: —— quo turbine cestum Sauromates, falcémque Getes.

page.notes: Woodcut of a helmeted soldier with shield and curved sword, set in the left part of the text block; not transcribed. Left edge shows strips of text from the facing page, not transcribed. The mark after "vice" is a curved sign, read as printed. The Greek "τῖς" after "τὴν αὐτὴν" is uncertain. Its article may be "τῆς", so it is marked [?]. The Greek "στρατιωτῶν" is set with a worn initial and may read differently. "Ij" is printed as such. The "»" before "Ad Orientalem" is a printed sign, kept.
